To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new computational depth sensing approach that can be used for high-speed and high-accuracy depth sensing with commodity hardware.

we have developed a new computational depth sensing approach that is based on structured light, but that does not need to project a sequence of patterns, and that can produce real-time, high-resolution, high-quality depth.
we have proposed and demonstrated several computational depth sensors that are based on a single image, a single pattern, or a single camera.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions:     1.
the development of high-performance, low-cost structured light cameras.

the design of a new generation of depth cameras that can achieve high performance at low cost and low power, and that can operate in real-time with high accuracy, high resolution, and robustness to ambient light.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no existing depth camera is able to achieve high-performance depth sensing with a single camera, in a cost-effective manner.
there is no single depth camera that is best for all applications.
there is no one-size-fits-all camera for depth sensing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a computational depth camera that can achieve a high frame rate (30 fps) with high resolution (640×480) and high accuracy (±1 mm) by using a single light pattern and a single camera.

we have proposed and developed new algorithms and systems to address the aforementioned limitations of the mainstream depth cameras and enable a new generation of high-performance commodity depth sensors.

, we are trying to make depth sensing more affordable by using commodity cameras, such as off-the-shelf RGB cameras and light field cameras, and by designing algorithms to improve the performance of depth sensing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed an efficient and effective computational depth-sensing framework that enables commodity cameras to achieve high-resolution depth sensing in real-time.
the computational approach is an effective way of addressing the aforementioned challenges in the depth sensing domain, especially for commodity structured light cameras.
we can achieve real-time depth with high resolution and accuracy using a single pattern.
